message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (C allele) in Europeans**

| Population | Frequency (C allele) |
|------------|----------------------|
| 1000 Genomes – European (EUR) overall | **≈ 12 %** |
| 1000 Genomes – CEU (Utah residents of Northern/Western European ancestry) | ≈ 12 % |
| 1000 Genomes – TSI (Toscani in Italy) | ≈ 10 % |
| 1000 Genomes – IBS (Iberian Spanish) | ≈ 13 % |

> **Interpretation**  
> The rs7412 SNP is one of two key variants that define the APOE ε2, ε3, and ε4 alleles. In most European cohorts, the C allele (which defines ε2) occurs at roughly 10–13 % of chromosomes, while the T allele (defining ε3 and ε4) is the major allele (~87–90 %).  

> **Sources**  
> * 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 (European superpopulation, EUR) – allele counts for rs7412.  
> * ExAC / gnomAD (European subset) – allele frequency estimates consistent with 1000 Genomes.  

> **Notes**  
> * Frequencies can vary slightly between sub‑European groups (e.g., Northern vs. Southern Europe).  
> * The allele frequency is often reported as the proportion of chromosomes carrying the C allele; genotype frequencies can be derived assuming Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium if needed.  

If you need the exact allele counts or genotype frequencies for a specific subpopulation, let me know!
